title: CVS ExtraCare Rewards — quarterly ExtraBucks Rewards (program)
offer_text: Every time you make a purchase, either online or in-store, you'll earn ExtraCare program rewards, or ExtraBucks Rewards. Every 3 months your ExtraBucks Rewards will print on your store register receipt, or you can view, print and redeem your ExtraBucks Rewards online. — ExtraBucks Rewards are issued quarterly — on January 1st, April 1st, July 1st and October 1st. You can use your quarterly ExtraBucks Rewards for in-store or online purchases.
expiry_basis: Standing program. Rewards are issued on a fixed quarterly calendar (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1) and carry their own printed expiry.
requirements: Rewards print on the register receipt at a physical CVS store, or are viewed and printed online
Check the expiration date printed on each reward before use

bay_area.note: CVS Pharmacy operates many stores across San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose and the surrounding counties; ExtraBucks Rewards are explicitly usable in store and print at the register or at the in-store ExtraCare Coupon Center.

title: CVS ExtraCare Pharmacy & Health Rewards — $5 ExtraBucks per 10 credits, up to $50/year
offer_text: When you enroll in the ExtraCare Pharmacy & Health Rewards program and accumulate ten credits by purchasing eligible prescriptions or engaging in an eligible activity at a CVS Pharmacy in the U.S., you will receive $5 Pharmacy & Health ExtraBucks Rewards at CVS Pharmacy stores in the U.S. or on CVS.com. Ways to earn credits: purchasing a 30-day supply of an eligible prescription (1 credit); purchasing a 90-day supply of an eligible prescription (3 credits); receiving a flu shot or other vaccination from a CVS pharmacist (3 credits); enrolling in prescription management services on CVS.com (3 credits); enrolling a member on your ExtraCare card in the Program (1 credit per enrollment, limited to 5 per ExtraCare card). An individual can earn up to $50 Pharmacy & Health ExtraBucks Rewards in a calendar year. Rewards balances will be reset on December 31 each year.
expiry_basis: Standing program; annual reward cap resets and balances are reset every December 31.
requirements: Enroll in ExtraCare Pharmacy & Health Rewards (separate opt-in from ExtraCare)
Accumulate 10 credits from prescriptions, vaccinations or eligible activities
Reward prints on the receipt or at the in-store ExtraCare Coupon Center, roughly one week after it is earned
Up to $50 per individual per calendar year

bay_area.note: Redeemed at any CVS Pharmacy store, including the many Bay Area locations with in-store pharmacies. A flu shot at a Bay Area CVS pharmacy earns 3 of the 10 credits needed.

sources.title: ExtraCare Pharmacy & Health Rewards® Program Rules
sources.evidence: Credit values, reward amount, annual cap and reset date read verbatim from the official program rules, including 'you will receive $5 Pharmacy & Health ExtraBucks Rewards' after accumulating 'ten credits', 'An individual can earn up to $50 Pharmacy & Health ExtraBucks Rewards in a calendar year', and 'Rewards balances will be reset on December 31 each year.'

sources.evidence: Conflicting text on CVS's own help page: 'Each person sharing an ExtraCare card doesn't have to earn 4 credits before receiving $2 ExtraBucks Rewards ... Your $2 ExtraBucks Rewards will be issued approximately 1 week after every 4 credits have been earned ... Each person can earn $50 ExtraBucks Rewards per year through the rewards at the pharmacy benefit.'

checks: Reward mechanics read verbatim from the issuer's formal program rules
Cross-checked against a second official CVS page and a contradiction was found (see flags)

flags.detail: Two official CVS pages state different reward thresholds for the same program. The formal Program Rules page says 10 credits earn a $5 reward. The CVS help page says every 4 credits earn $2. Both agree the annual cap is $50 and that balances reset on December 31. Because the issuer contradicts itself, the practical earn rate must be confirmed with the pharmacist before relying on a specific figure. This dataset quotes both pages verbatim rather than choosing one silently.
Requires a separate authorization per person; individuals 16 and older must sign separately, and parents or guardians sign for children under 16.
Pharmacy rewards programs involve health data. Review CVS's privacy terms before opting in.

offer_text: Prescription Prices, Coupons & Pharmacy Information — GoodRx. GoodRx is NOT insurance.

verified_price_examples.drug: Wegovy® tablet, pen, and HD pen

expiry_basis: Prices are quoted 'as low as' and change with pharmacy and dosage; no fixed expiry is published.
requirements: Present the GoodRx coupon (print or app) at a participating pharmacy
GoodRx is not insurance and cannot be combined with insurance on the same fill

bay_area.note: GoodRx coupons are redeemed at the physical pharmacy counter. Participating chains with Bay Area pharmacy counters include CVS, Walgreens, Safeway and Costco Pharmacy, as well as independent Bay Area pharmacies.

sources.title: Prescription Prices, Coupons & Pharmacy Information - GoodRx
sources.evidence: Page title and disclaimer read verbatim: 'Prescription Prices, Coupons & Pharmacy Information - GoodRx' and 'GoodRx is NOT insurance'. Price examples read verbatim from the homepage cards: 'Foundayo™ As low as $149', 'Zepbound® KwikPen and others As low as $299', 'Wegovy® Tablet, pen, and HD pen As low as $149'. Paid plan text read verbatim: 'GoodRx Companion New 250+ free medications Plus hundreds more medications under $10. All for $9.99/month (when paid yearly).' and 'Plans from $9.99/mo for you, or $16.99/mo for up to 5 people and pets, when paid yearly.'

checks: Service, disclaimer and current homepage price examples read verbatim from the provider's own site
Paid-tier pricing ($9.99/mo individual, $16.99/mo family, when paid yearly) read verbatim from the same page
Prices recorded as 'as low as' figures exactly as the provider states them, not as guaranteed prices

flags.detail: The dollar figures are the provider's own 'as low as' marketing prices for specific drugs, dosage forms and quantities. The actual price at a specific Bay Area pharmacy depends on the drug, dose, quantity and pharmacy. No figure here should be treated as a guaranteed price.
GoodRx states prominently on its own homepage: 'GoodRx is NOT insurance'. Using a GoodRx coupon means paying cash prices instead of running insurance.

The free coupon service is separate from the paid 'GoodRx Companion' plan ($9.99/month when paid yearly, or $16.99/month for up to 5 people and pets). The '250+ free medications' claim belongs to the PAID plan, not to the free coupon service — an easy detail to misreport.
